text.p: Bonds closed near to their highs for the day as the market bet on the Federal Reserve leaving rates unchanged at its Open Market Committee meeting later on Tuesday.
If expectations were proved right, the market could gain further on Wednesday, traders said.

"The Bund led the advance and our 10 years followed," said one trader. "The curve closed well-supported and if the Fed does nothing, it is going to rise more because Europe is technically strong," he added.
Traders said that Portugal should accompany any fresh advance in the German Bunds where the market was relieved that the Bundesbank left its repo unchanged and by the better than expected M3 figures.
There was investment interest from end-users at the shorter end of the curve up to the five years after the Bank of Portugal's rate cut on Monday, traders added.
